subject: physics
question_text: Two bodies undergo a perfectly inelastic head-on collision. Obtain expressions for their common velocity and for the loss of kinetic energy.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The common velocity
lines: In a perfectly inelastic collision the bodies
move on together with one velocity v.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the bodies move on together before writing the momentum equation.
steps.why: Momentum is conserved in EVERY collision; kinetic energy is not. Starting from the conserved quantity is what makes this answer short.
common_mistakes: Using conservation of kinetic energy here; it is exactly what does not hold.

recall.must_convey: That the bodies move together and momentum conservation gives v equal to m one u one plus m two u two over m one plus m two.
accept: they move together with one velocity
m one u one plus m two u two over m one plus m two
reject: half m one u one squared

steps.memory_tip: v is the total momentum divided by the total mass — a weighted average of u₁ and u₂.

steps.label: The two energies
lines: After it the two move as one body:
Substituting v from the first step gives K_f
in terms of the starting velocities.
steps.margin_note: Two marks, one for each energy. Write K_i and K_f in full before you subtract.
steps.why: Writing both energies before subtracting keeps the algebra honest; substituting v too early is where mistakes usually happen.
common_mistakes: Writing K_f with the two masses moving at different speeds after a perfectly inelastic collision.

recall.must_convey: That K initial is half m one u one squared plus half m two u two squared and K final is half of the total mass times v squared.
accept: half m one u one squared plus half m two u two squared
half m one plus m two into v squared
reject: they move together with one velocity

steps.memory_tip: Two ½mu² terms before, ONE ½(m₁ + m₂)v² term after. Two bodies in, one moving body out.

steps.label: The loss
lines: This is always positive, so kinetic energy is
always lost. It turns into heat and sound.
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Box the loss, then say where the energy went — heat and sound.
steps.why: The loss depends on the RELATIVE velocity, so two bodies moving at the same velocity lose nothing — the (u₁ − u₂)² factor shows the collision has to be a real one.
common_mistakes: Concluding energy is destroyed; it is converted, not destroyed.

recall.must_convey: That the loss is half times the reduced mass times the square of the relative velocity, always positive, appearing as heat and sound.
accept: half m one m two over m one plus m two into u one minus u two squared
reject: K initial is half m one u one squared

steps.memory_tip: It is ½μ(u₁ − u₂)² with the reduced mass μ = m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂) — the same ½mv² shape.

insider_note: The two energies carry 2 of the 4 marks. Write both in full before subtracting; skipping straight to ΔK loses them.
